chunks: Humeed ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who died and left a slave boy, so one of the inheritors testified that he was free. He said: If the witness is reliable, his testimony is accepted for his share, and he is asked to work (or compensate) for what belongs to the other inheritors.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's emancipation if one heir testifies he is free?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of partial emancipation (tadbir) in Shia jurisprudence, where a reliable heir's testimony validates the slave's freedom only for his proportional share of the estate. For the remaining shares belonging to other heirs, the slave must work or pay compensation, reflecting the practical application of inheritance law and the importance of witness credibility (riwāyah) in resolving financial disputes among co-heirs.

en.hubeali:
Hameed Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from one of his companions, from Aban Bin Usman, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who died and left an owned slave. So one of the inheritors testifies that he is free. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he was present during illness, his testimony is allowed with regards to his share, and he (the slave) would have to work with regards to what was for the others from the inheritors’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from certain persons of his people from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Mansur ibn Hazim who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who dies and leaves behind an owned slave, but certain ones of the heirs testify that he is free.

He (the Imam) said, ‘If the testifying person is an acceptable person his testimony is permissible on his share of the legacy and the slave is made to work to buy his freedom from the rest of the heirs.’”
